proof.bench: results/die_kv_26_1029/rst/bench_kv_reset.sh (MUT 0 KVRST_PASS min 20 locked edges in reset at a START-gated rgate tap, 22 at an rsync landing; MUT 1 lock qualifier STABLE 4 and MUT 2 lock qualifier bypassed both FATAL)

generator: bound KV die root (bind26b kv3_hub_C_part.sv u_rst_root/u_rst_lockq, por_gate PASS): pad por_n -> ot_dp_rsync_s2 (async assert, 2-clock release) -> ot_dp_lockq STABLE 16 (2-flop lock sync + 16 consecutive locked cycles, synchronously cleared by d): the root reset stays asserted >= 1 + 2 + 16 + 1 locked own-clock edges after ANY arm (power-on, mid-run por_n pulse of any width; lock loss during reset restarts the count)
sinks: every KV core reset pin is a wavefront tap of that root: ot_dp_rrelay chains (synchronous, width-preserving delay), ot_dp_rgate START-gated consumer taps (q <= d & run: release no earlier than the relay) or ot_dp_rsync spine landings (async assert, S-clock release): each holds reset at least as long as the root window with the die clock running. bench DEPTH 8 (bind_reset max release 97 only delays the window).
modules_basis: every hard-core module of KV plan event26/event26a (30 modules at event26; PC -> PCC + PCF split per pc_split_basis, incl. kv3_astk); a kit LEC may use OT_LEC_RESET_CYCLES <= 16
kit_use: copy reset_contract.json + reset_contract/receipt.txt into KIT/ (receipt path is relative), or set OT_LEC_RESET_CONTRACT to this file
scope: mid-run reset re-assertion follows the same contract (bench: 8 por_n pulses 0.05..1.94 ns at 8 phases + lock loss inside a reset). A lock loss AFTER release does not re-arm the die reset (ot_dp_lockq sticky, HOST status) and is not a reset event.
pc_split_basis: DIE-KV-67 11-04, COORD ruling (b): qkd_kvs_pc / qkd_kvs_pc_h_head_p left this list, their rst_n and hrst_n came from a reset-less data lane the DIE-KV-26 proof does not cover. The PC split parents drive every PCC / PCF rst_n and hrst_n through ot_dp_rgate (q <= lane & wavefront tap, bind core_splits reset_gate, rst_n_t relay nearest the core): q stays low while the tap is low, so each pin holds reset at least the proven root window whatever the lane does. By construction from the rgate source; no new bench was run.
pc_rgate_soft_note: DIE-KV-95 11-08: the 6 kv3_pc* partition types are listed because their 9 soft-leaf reset pins go through ot_dp_rgate (reset_gate_bindings, lane AND wavefront tap), the same by-construction argument as pc_split_basis; pilot cl254f2e73 at 16 edges 457 -> 43 differ, 236 missing -> 0
types_basis: KV-PLAN-2 11-10 (COORD: kv3_hg 2b151cb27bf2 FAIL_PREFLOOR LEC NOT EQUIVALENT, same rule as QC DIE-QC-59 11-01 and S81 S81-KVLEAF-LEC-1 11-07): every partition type module of the KV plan of record (kw43/kvr2 plan_c 92370701, 56 types). Their generated wrapper reset pins (arst_n / rst_root_n and the bind's cland_reset / rst_rl relays) are wavefront taps of the same bound KV die root (ot_dp_rsync_s2 + ot_dp_lockq STABLE 16): synchronous, width-preserving ot_dp_rrelay chains or START-gated ot_dp_rgate taps, so each holds reset at least the proven root window. Type kits otherwise ran the 4-edge default: kv3_hg 1604 differs, all in the embedded astk u_exp no-reset pipeline registers (g_h[].u_m.u.u_c1/u_c2.g_r.r, u_ca.g_r.r, s1_rows, d_lo.g_line.line) that kv3_astk itself proves EQUIVALENT only at 16 edges (DIE-KV-65).
